summary: Design public agricultural shock-financing programmes, triggers, and delivery plans. Review the course outline and explore enrolment options.
lede: Disaster risk financing for agriculture covers how public programme and finance professionals plan funding and farmer support for shocks. Participants assess agricultural exposure and data gaps, map financing layers, compare insurance and contingent finance, and draft triggers and activation plans. They also develop budget-linked delivery, expenditure-tracking, and monitoring plans using the World Bank Disaster Risk Financing and Insurance framework and FAO agricultural risk tools.
audienceIntro: This intermediate course suits professionals who shape or operate public agricultural support before and after climate and disaster shocks. It is designed for roles with responsibility for budgets, risk information, insurance, programme delivery, or farmer services.
modules: Sendai Framework and Agricultural Programme Mandates
FAO ASIS and Agricultural Risk Analysis
Integrated Financing Plan and Progress Reporting
prerequisites: Prior experience in public programme delivery, agricultural finance, disaster risk management, public budgeting, insurance, or agricultural services is expected. No coding or programming is required. Familiarity with spreadsheets is useful for the Excel-based financing and tracking exercises.
